sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: The report targets 15-year-old students (aged 15 years 3 months to 16 years 2 months) enrolled in grade 7 or above, with at least 6 years of formal schooling, regardless of institution type and whether full-time or part-time. It applies strict technical standards for inclusion/exclusion, with an overall exclusion rate within a country required to be below 5% to limit distortion of national mean scores; exclusions can occur at the school level (e.g., remote/inaccessible, very small schools, operational factors) or at the student level (e.g., intellectual disability or limited proficiency in the language of the assessment). The excerpt also notes that some countries used paper-based delivery for trend items, while the main survey was computer-based, and that the collaborative problem-solving assessment was not administered in all countries.

data.outcome_summary: PISA 2015 Volume I focuses on science as the major domain, with reading and mathematics as additional core domains and collaborative problem solving as a minor domain for participating countries. The assessment is delivered mainly via computer (with paper-based options for some countries limited to trend-measuring items), and each student completes a two-hour test composed of four 30-minute clusters; for science, clusters include both trend and new science items. Students also complete a student background questionnaire (about 35 minutes), while school principals complete a school questionnaire (about 45 minutes), with optional teacher and parent questionnaires in some systems. The report presents results as proficiency distributions across science levels (including a baseline level expected for all students by the end of compulsory education) and discusses equity by socio-economic status and immigrant background. It emphasizes that PISA cannot identify cause-and-effect relationships between policies and outcomes, but it provides robust cross-country comparisons and trend information using PISA’s scaling and linking procedures.
